title: How to Invest Safely in Retirement (Bonds, Dividend Funds, TIPS)
content:
Investing in retirement requires a complete psychological shift. For 40 years, your goal was 'Growth.' Now, your goal is 'Income and Stability.' You no longer have a paycheck to replace investment losses. However, going to 100% cash is also risky because inflation will destroy your purchasing power over a 30-year retirement. The solution is a 'Safety-First' portfolio that secures your basic needs with guaranteed income while leaving a portion in stocks for long-term growth.

Key Takeaways

  • The 'Floor' Strategy: Cover your essential expenses (Food, Housing, Medical) with guaranteed income sources: Social Security, Pensions, and Bond Ladders. Never risk your grocery money in the stock market.
  • TIPS (Inflation Protection): Treasury Inflation-Protected Securities are the retiree's best friend. The principal adjusts with CPI, guaranteeing you don't fall behind cost-of-living increases.
  • Dividend Growth: Instead of selling shares for income, build a portfolio of 'Dividend Aristocrats' (companies that raise payouts annually). This provides a rising paycheck without touching the principal.
  • The Bucket System: Keep 2-3 years of cash in a 'Liquidity Bucket' to ride out bear markets. You never want to be a forced seller of stocks when the market is down.

Why It Matters (US Context)

The '4% Rule' relies on a mix of stocks and bonds. In 2025, with interest rates normalized, bonds are once again a viable income generator. A 10-year Treasury yielding 4% provides a safe floor that wasn't available in the 2010s.

The Retirement Asset Menu

Build your portfolio with these building blocks.

1. Fixed Income (Safety)

  • Individual Bond Ladder: Buy Treasuries maturing in 2026, 2027, 2028. You know exactly how much cash will arrive each year.
  • Short-Term Bond Funds (BSV): Low volatility, decent yield. Good for money needed in 3-5 years.
  • TIPS (VTIP): Allocate 20% of bond portfolio here to hedge against unexpected inflation spikes.

2. Equity Income (Growth)

  • Dividend Growth (VIG/SCHD): Companies with strong cash flows. Less volatile than Tech. Provides a 'raise' every year.
  • Equity Income (VYM): Higher current yield, slower growth. Good if you need cash now.

3. Cash Equivalents (Sleep)

Money Market Funds (VMFXX): Keep 1-2 years of spending here. This is your moat. If the market crashes 50%, you ignore it and live off this cash.

Sample Allocation for Age 65

  1. The 'Balanced' Retiree: 50% Stocks / 50% Bonds. Historically safe withdrawal rate of ~4%. Capture growth but halve the volatility of the market.
  2. The 'Income' Focus: 30% Stocks / 70% Bonds. Lower returns, but very stable income. Good if you have a large portfolio and don't need high growth to survive.
  3. The 'Barbell': 80% Safe Assets (TIPS/Cash) to cover all basic needs. 20% High Risk (Tech/Small Cap) for 'Play Money' or legacy for heirs.

Frequently Asked Questions

Should I buy an annuity?

A Single Premium Immediate Annuity (SPIA) is a valid bond replacement. You trade a lump sum for a guaranteed paycheck for life. It hedges 'Longevity Risk' (living to 105).

Are high-yield bonds safe?

No. 'Junk Bonds' correlate with stocks. In a recession, they crash. Keep your bonds high quality (Treasuries/Investment Grade Corporate) to act as a true hedge.

Do I need international stocks?

Yes, for diversification. But retirees often lower their international allocation (e.g., to 10-15%) to reduce currency risk volatility.
